title: Dependability Studio charter and 90-day experiment slate
content:
Purpose

This doc defines the "Dependability Studio": a lightweight, cross-functional working group (SRE + serving runtime + platform engineering + product-hosted-api + solutions eng) focused on rapid experiments to reduce reliability risk and operational cost for model-serving workloads over a 90-day horizon. The Studio is intentionally tactical — run short experiments, capture signals (latency, error surface, cost per 1k tokens), iterate, and hand off proven patterns to product/engineering for standardization.

Why a Studio?
- We repeatedly hit unknowns at the intersection of model behavior, batching, cache effectiveness, and regional capacity fallbacks.
- Traditional long-form projects are slow; we need a forum to run controlled, measurable experiments, learn quickly, and share reproducible playbooks.
- Studio reduces cognitive hand-off friction: experiments include engineers, oncall SREs, product owners, and a solutions engineer so results are deployable.

High-level goals (90 days)
1) Produce 3 reproducible reliability interventions that reduce P99 latency or error-rate impact during degraded nodes by >=15% (measured on canary traffic).
2) Create a minimal SLO-pattern library for model-serving use cases (chat-streaming, embeddings, reranking) with templates for alerting and error budgets.
3) Run an ops tabletop with product and sales to validate communication playbooks for customer-impacting degradations.

Studio scope and out-of-scope
- In scope: model-serving runtime behaviors (KV cache eviction policies, batching heuristics), routing fallbacks between model sizes, canary traffic experiments, observability signal curation for SLOs.
- Out of scope: wholesale model training, core billing system changes, long-term infra procurement (those escalate to dedicated capacity projects).

Roles and commitments
- Studio Lead (Aisha Patel): convener, prioritization, and blocking removal. 0.2 FTE.
- SRE Lead (Ethan Liu): operational validation, runbook updates, oncall engagement. 0.1–0.2 FTE.
- Serving Runtime Engineer (Oliver Reed): implements experiment hooks, lightweight feature flags, kernel selection toggles. 0.3 FTE during active experiments.
- Product/PO (Priya Nair): decides acceptance criteria, customer context, and escalates rollouts. 0.05 FTE.
- Rotating participants: solutions engineering, support engineer, dedicated customer owner when experiment relates to a tenant.

Meeting cadence
- Weekly 45-minute sync: experiment progress, signal review, unblockers. Fast decisions only.
- Biweekly demo: 15-minute demo + 15-minute lessons learned (open invite).
- Monthly stakeholder review (leadership summary + ask).

Experiment intake and prioritization
- Intake form (short): hypothesis, acceptance metrics, required data access, rollback criteria, owner, expected duration. Link: CONFLUENCE-1234/Dependability-Studio-Intake (placeholder).
- Prioritization axes: customer impact, risk reduction per engineering hour, measurability, dependencies.
- Minimum viable experiment definition: must have an automated metric collection pipeline and a clear canary rollout path (<= 5% traffic).

90-day experiment slate (initial, subject to weekly reprioritization)
Experiment A: Adaptive prefix caching eviction policy
- Hypothesis: switching to an LRU with frequency-awareness for prefix keys will reduce repetitive KV misses for streaming chat customers and cut P99 token latency by >=12% on mid-length sessions (20–120 tokens).
- Owner: Oliver Reed
- Acceptance: synthetic benchmark + canary on internal traffic showing P95/P99 latency improvement and no increase in downstream error rate over 72h.
- Risk controls: feature flag, instant rollback, isolated cache namespace for canary.

Experiment B: QoS routing to fall back to quantized model variants under GPU pressure
- Hypothesis: routing short-latency-sensitive requests to a smaller quantized variant when cluster load > 80% reduces request timeouts and keeps observed error budget burn < 50% during surge windows.
- Owner: Platform Eng rep (TBD) + SRE
- Acceptance: canary across region with cost/latency/error tradeoff dashboard; SLO burn tracking baseline vs. experiment.

Experiment C: Continuous micro-batching windows for embeddings pipelines
- Hypothesis: a small adaptive micro-batching window (20–50ms) yields >=25% GPU throughput improvement for embeddings while keeping tail latency SLAs for interactive flows.
- Owner: Serving Runtime
- Acceptance: end-to-end embeddings job throughput increase on representative workload; no customer-visible tail latency regression.

Experiment D (ops/tabletop): Communication playbook + friction test
- Hypothesis: a pre-baked external communication template and a 30-min exec escalation rehearsal will reduce mean time to external notification from 2.5 hours to < 30 minutes during P1 incidents involving model degradation.
- Owner: SRE Lead + Customer Success rep
- Acceptance: tabletop executed with product and CS, checklist updated, timing measured.

Measurement and observability
- Core signals to capture per experiment: P50/P95/P99 latency (token-level where possible), total errors (by class), request timeout counts, autoscaler activity, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens estimate, SLO burn rate.
- Minimum instrumentation: a dashboard per experiment (Grafana) and an automated daily digest posted to #dependability-studio Slack channel.
- Regression guardrails: any increase in user-visible error rate or SLO burn causes immediate experiment halt.

Runbook / handoff
- For experiments that meet acceptance, we produce: 1) an operations runbook (play steps for incidents), 2) a PRD-lite for productization, 3) a rollout plan (canary -> phased).
- Hand-off criteria: reproducible results across two canary windows separated by 7 days, automated tests covering the change, and documented rollback steps.

Decision authority and escalation
- Studio Lead can greenlight experiments and short-term rollouts up to 5% traffic change. Anything beyond requires SRE + Product signoff.
- If an experiment causes SLO burn beyond threshold, SRE Lead has unilateral rollback authority.

Budget and resource note
- Initial budget: low (team time). If experiment requires sustained dedicated GPU capacity for >7 days, open a cost bucket request with platform-engineering. Track spent hours in the intake form.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: noisy metrics from synthetic vs production traffic. Mitigation: prefer small production canaries over synthetic-only validation.
- Risk: experiment churn without productization. Mitigation: gate studio experiments with a productization checklist.

Open questions (to decide in next 2 weeks)
- Ownership model for experiment artifacts: should the Studio maintain a short-lived repo or do we put artifacts in the serving-runtime repo?
- What's the SLA for demo-to-productization handoff? Proposed: 30 days to PRD-lite or archive with reasons.
- How do we credit cross-functional time in team planning cycles? Corporate HR/people ops input needed.

Next steps (first 30 days)
- Finalize intake form + automate template dashboards (Ethan, Oliver)
- Kickoff Experiment A with small internal canary (week 1)
- Schedule first tabletop rehearsal (week 3)
- Create a single Slack channel (#dependability-studio) and calendar series for weekly syncs (Aisha)

Notes to self / working bits
- Quick links to prototypes and repos: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/exp/prefix-cache-proto (WIP).
- Consider embedding a lightweight chaos script to simulate KV store hiccups for more robust tests.

Appendix: simple acceptance checklist (copyable)
- Hypothesis written and measurable metric identified.
- Data collection and dashboard present.
- Canary rollout path defined and flagged.
- Rollback/runbook written.
- Product/owner signoff for handoff or archive.

-- end of draft --

(Feedback welcome — this is intentionally concise and tactical; we can expand to include a sample dashboard layout and a postmortem template if people want it.)
